subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II, DPA & confirmation of EU/UK processing boundary
messages:
From: Elena Moroz <elena.moroz@fintrust.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 09:15 BST
Subject: Request: SOC 2 Type II and data processing jurisdiction details

Hi Rachel,

We are kicking off procurement and legal review for a pilot with Redwood and need the following before our procurement committee call on Sep 25:

- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period) and a short cover note describing the audit period.
- Confirmation of where customer data (prompts, responses, embeddings) are processed and stored for a Hosted account provisioned for an EU customer: specifically, do any customer content or metadata copies exist outside the EU/UK?
- Any supplemental attestation or statement you can provide that delineates the processing boundary for EU/UK customers (short signed statement preferred).
- Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and confirmation you will execute SCCs / EU Standard Contractual Clauses if needed.
- List of controls/evidence we can request: encryption at rest, access logs, retention policy, log retention window, and SOC 2 control mapping (which controls cover customer data residency).

Can you confirm the SOC 2 audit period (start / end dates) and whether the policy for control-plane metadata is considered part of the scope for EU-hosted customers? If you can respond by EOD Sep 20 that would keep us on schedule.

Thanks,
Elena Moroz
Senior Counsel, FinTrust
elena.moroz@fintrust.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-18 16:40 EDT
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: SOC 2 Type II and data processing jurisdiction details

Rachel / Markus — quick answers:

1) SOC 2 Type II: coverage period Sep 1, 2025 — Aug 31, 2026. We have the final auditor attestation and report (PDF).

2) Hosted behavior: For customers who select an EU region we process and store the customer content (prompts, responses, embeddings) in the selected EU region for inference and storage. However, the control plane (account metadata, telemetry, and aggregated logs used for billing/usage) is currently in our US control plane. We do not persist customer content copies to US for routine processing. There are two caveats:
  - In support cases, engineers can request temporary diagnostic copies for debugging; those are on a least-privilege basis and access-controlled and logged.
  - Some system-level telemetry and anonymized aggregates may leave the EU for operational monitoring.

3) Attestation: Legal & InfoSec can produce a 1-page "processing boundary statement" that clarifies the above and states that for EU-hosted accounts customer content is stored and processed in EU regions and is not copied to US as a matter of routine. We will need FinTrust to sign an NDA for any exceptional diagnostic copies if they want those restricted.

4) Artifacts we can deliver by Sep 20: SOC2 PDF (final), DPA v3 (fillable, we execute SCCs), SCC template, a short encryption-at-rest and key management note, and an access-logging statement. The processing_boundary_statement_draft.pdf attached by Rachel is fine to refine; we can produce a signed PDF.

Attachments: internal: SOC2 stub, DPA v3 link (internal).

Naomi
Head of Compliance Operations

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moroz <elena.moroz@fintrust.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20 08:17 BST
Subject: Re: Request: SOC 2 Type II and data processing jurisdiction details

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Below is what we can share and the next steps; I cc'd our Compliance and Security leads so they are on the thread.

1) SOC 2 Type II report: attached (redwood_soc2_type2_2026.pdf). Audit period covered in the report: Sep 1, 2025 — Aug 31, 2026.

2) Processing boundary for EU-hosted accounts:
  - Customer content (prompts, responses, embeddings) provisioned to an EU region account is stored and served from that EU region.
  - Control plane metadata (account IDs, anonymized telemetry and billing metadata) is maintained in our US control plane. We do not routinely replicate customer content to the US.
  - Exceptional diagnostic copies: we can create temporary, access-controlled copies for troubleshooting under customer authorization; these are logged and time-limited.

3) Attestation / written statement: We have attached a draft "processing_boundary_statement_draft.pdf". Naomi has confirmed Compliance can prepare a signed 1-page attestation that makes the above explicit; we can provide it by Sep 22.

4) DPA and SCCs: Attached is our current DPA template (redwood_data_processing_addendum_v3.docx). We are happy to execute SCCs and have a standard clause set we add for EU customers.

5) Evidence list we can provide: encryption-at-rest note, KMS integration description, access logging statement, SOC2 control map, and export of retention policy. Let me know which specific artifacts you need for legal review and we'll prioritize.

Proposed next step: quick 30-min call with you + FinTrust procurement on Sep 22 (we are available 09:00-12:00 BST) to walk through the SOC2 and the processing-boundary attestation.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_soc2_type2_2026.pdf, redwood_data_processing_addendum_v3.docx, processing_boundary_statement_draft.pdf
